title: Pelvic diaphragm: levator ani and coccygeus muscles (inferior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Back of the body of the pubis and the front part of the tendinous arch of levator ani.
Anococcygeal ligament and coccyx. Its inner fibers blend with the prostate or vagina, the perineal body, and the wall of the anal canal.
Nerve to levator ani (S4), with branches of the pudendal nerve.
With the rest of levator ani, supports the pelvic organs, resists rises in abdominal pressure, and helps keep the urethra and anal canal closed.
hy: Stretching or tearing of levator ani in childbirth weakens the pelvic floor and can lead to prolapse of the pelvic organs and stress urinary incontinence.

rows: Tendinous arch of levator ani and the ischial spine.
Nerve to levator ani (S4), with branches of the pudendal nerve.
With the rest of levator ani, supports the pelvic organs and raises the pelvic floor.
Side of the lower sacrum and the coccyx.
Anterior rami of S4 and S5.
Supports the pelvic organs as the back part of the pelvic floor and flexes the coccyx.
Posterior ilium, lateral sacrum, and coccyx to the ischial tuberosity.
With the sacrospinous ligament it turns the sciatic notches into foramina and resists upward tilting of the lower sacrum under the weight of the trunk.
Margins of the obturator foramen, closing it except for the obturator canal at the top.
Gives origin to obturator internus and obturator externus. The obturator nerve and vessels leave the pelvis through the obturator canal.
Large bone of the pelvic girdle, formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium, and pubis at the acetabulum.
Sacrum at the sacroiliac joint, the other hip bone at the pubic symphysis, and the head of the femur at the acetabulum.
Iliac crest, anterior superior iliac spine, acetabulum, obturator foramen, ischial spine, ischial tuberosity, greater and lesser sciatic notches.
Five fused vertebrae forming the back of the pelvis, between the two hip bones.
L5 above, the coccyx below, and the ilium on each side at the sacroiliac joint.
Sacral promontory, anterior and posterior sacral foramina, the sacral canal, and the sacral hiatus.
Three to five small fused vertebrae at the lower end of the vertebral column (the tailbone).
Gives attachment to gluteus maximus, the muscles of the pelvic floor, and the anococcygeal ligament.
Midline joint between the bodies of the two pubic bones.
A disc of fibrocartilage (the interpubic disc), strengthened by the superior and inferior pubic ligaments.
Holds the front of the pelvic ring together and allows a little movement. It loosens in late pregnancy.
